output.title: When rounding becomes a workflow problem
output.body:
If “rounding claims” is just a vague complaint, it is hard to fix and easy to argue about. I would turn it into one bounded workflow question: where do small numerical gaps actually change what you do?

Think about one recurring case only: invoice rounding, currency conversion, timesheet variance, or an estimate-to-actual mismatch. Then map the control boundary. Which differences are already covered by policy, like rounding to the nearest cent? Which need a human decision, because the gap affects approval or the audit trail? Which have no rule yet? The point is not to automate everything. It is to separate invisible variance from visible variance.

The practical next step is simple: write one rule in plain English for one workflow. For example: “Round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” That gives you something concrete to test against the way you already work.

Ask yourself one diagnostic question: do I document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly yet, fix the policy first. The machine can wait; paperwork rarely does.
